description: Siemens SIPROTEC 5 7SL87 distance zones (function '21 Distance prot.1', zones Z1..Zn) as a DIGSI 5 setting sheet prints them, with the DIGSI address written inside each setting name (21.901.357n.xxx). Catalog-only. Configured settings: per-zone Mode (status), Directional mode, Function mode (loops), X reach, R (ph-g), Zone-inclination angle (tilt), zone-specific Kr / Kx, the CT / VT ratings, the Edit-mode basis and the line data. Documented relay behaviour (DEC-198, Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, V07.50, version-dependent for the 7SL87_8.81 sheet): the quadrilateral characteristic of every enabled zone stated with the quadrilateral parameter set (no selector exists), R (ph-ph) / R (ph-g) as per-phase values, and the operate-delay loop assignment. Source-data gaps: the operating-delay setting cells on the sheet are blank (Infinity is printed in the range column), so every delay is Missing. Not representable (blocking): the resistance boundary inclined at the distance characteristic angle (exact relation preserved; no vertical +R mapped unless the angle is 90 deg) and the left / directional boundary. A non-zero Zone-inclination angle tilt is also exact-relation-preserved -- since 1.2.0 derived as a canonical tilted upper reactance boundary in SHADOW mode only, per zone, added alongside the zone's plain top (DEC-199 Phase 2D; production unchanged). A full shadow zone cannot yet be assembled for any 7SL87 zone: the left resistive boundary is not established from verified sources (see above), so `assemble_zone` is never called for this catalog. Not yet verified (blocking while in use): the phase-phase load cutout's effect on the zone.
interpretation_notes: Zone N is the zone 'Z N' of function '21 Distance prot.1' (DIGSI addresses 21.901.357N.xxx); the numbering follows the sheet.
The sheet's Edit mode is Primary: the impedance values on the sheet are primary ohms.

Every operating delay (1-phase and multi-phase) has a blank setting cell; the 'Infinity' beside it is the range column, not a configured delay. No delay is assumed, and the document notes' timers are not used.

Documented relay behaviour (Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, SIPROTEC 5 manual V07.50, 6.6 Distance protection with classic method): each distance zone is a zone function block of one operate-curve type -- quadrilateral, quadrilateral with adaptive pickup, MHO or circular (6.6.2.2) -- and the device has no characteristic selector. A zone stated with X reach, R (ph-g), R (ph-ph) and Zone-inclination angle is a quadrilateral zone (MHO and circular zones are set by Zr impedance reach). The reference is V07.50; the owner sheet is scheme 7SL87_8.81: applicability rests on the matching function and parameter structure and is version-dependent, not a firmware match.

Documented phase-phase geometry (per-phase R-X plane, forward zone): top X <= X reach, inclined by the Zone-inclination angle in the first quadrant (0 deg = horizontal, drawn exactly); right Rright(X) = R (ph-ph) + X * cot(phi), the resistance line inclined at the distance characteristic angle phi (21.901.2311.107, common to all zones of the function) so that it runs parallel to the line impedance (6.6.15.4, Fig. 6-141). R (ph-ph) and R (ph-g) are per-phase (conductor / positive-sequence) values: the loop fault resistance is halved for R (ph-ph) and divided by (1 + Kr) for R (ph-g) (6.6.15.6). The left side of a forward zone is formed by the quadrilateral's own resistance limit and the device's fixed directional characteristic (6.6.4, Fig. 6-102), whose exact geometry is not established from the verified sources.

Geometry limitation: the current engine draws vertical resistive limits. With phi = 82.7 deg the inclined right boundary cannot be represented, so no Right (+R) Resistive Reach is plotted; the left / directional boundary is not represented either. No approximation is applied (candidate A7, +R = R (ph-ph), conservative with shortfall X * cot(phi) at the X reach, is documented only and not approved).

The load cutout (21.901.3661.1xx, Pickup Z<) removes the load area from the operate area (6.6.5). The phase-phase load cutout is in use on this sheet; its exact shape relative to the polygon (Fig. 6-106) is not yet verified, so its effect on an enabled zone is not established and it blocks. The phase-ground load cutout acts on the phase-earth loops, which the phase-phase engine does not draw.

boundaries.equation: X(R) = X reach - R * tan(Zone-inclination angle) for R >= 0, added alongside the plain top X <= X reach (Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.15.6: 'the limit of the X setting for Zone 1 is inclined downwards by the zone inclination'; the parameter is per-zone)

zone_preserved.reason: A zone operating / blocking switch of the vendor's scheme logic; it does not change the zone's geometry and is not interpreted.
K0 / Angle (K0) are the other residual-compensation format; this sheet is set to the Kr, Kx format (91.115). Preserved, not used.

Geometry-affecting: the phase-phase load cutout removes the load area (R load cutout, Angle load cutout) from the phase-phase operate area (Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.5). Its exact shape relative to this zone's polygon is not yet verified, so whether it cuts the zone is not established. Preserved, not drawn; not assumed to have no effect.

Geometry-affecting: the phase-phase load-cutout limits (minimum load resistance and opening angle) of the load area removed from the operate area. Preserved, not drawn; their effect on the zone is not yet verified.

Geometry-affecting for the phase-earth loops: the phase-ground load cutout removes the load area from the phase-ground operate area. The phase-phase engine does not draw the phase-earth loops. Preserved, not drawn.

mappings.note: A SIPROTEC 5 distance zone is a zone function block of one operate-curve type, and the device has no characteristic selector (Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.2.2). This zone is stated with the quadrilateral parameter set (X reach, R (ph-g), R (ph-ph), Zone-inclination angle; MHO and circular zones use Zr impedance reach), so it is a quadrilateral zone; applied to an enabled zone. The resistance lines are inclined at the distance characteristic angle, which the current engine does not reproduce.

not_exposed.note: SIPROTEC 5 has no characteristic selector: a zone's operate curve is fixed by the type of its zone function block.

mappings.note: Function mode states which loops the zone measures (Siemens options: ph-gnd and ph-ph, ph-gnd only, ph-ph only).
Function mode states which loops the zone measures (Siemens options: ph-gnd and ph-ph, ph-gnd only, ph-ph only).

The zone is stated as X and R limits (X reach, R (ph-ph), R (ph-g)), not as a polar reach. Its resistance boundaries are inclined at the distance characteristic angle, which this representation cannot carry (see the Right Resistive Reach (+R)).

gap.note: R (ph-ph) is documented as a per-phase (conductor / positive-sequence) resistance reach: it is not a loop value and is not halved (Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.15.6). The zone's resistance line is inclined at the distance characteristic angle phi, common to all zones, parallel to the line impedance (6.6.15.4): Rright(X) = R + X * cot(phi), with R = R (ph-ph) ({evidence}). The current engine draws only a vertical resistive limit (Rright = R), so this boundary cannot be represented exactly; no Right Resistive Reach (+R) is plotted and no approximation is applied. Only phi = 90 deg would make the boundary vertical.

requires.off_note: The distance characteristic angle is not 90 deg, so the resistance line is inclined and R (ph-ph) is not a vertical +R.
requires.missing_note: the distance characteristic angle (21.901.2311.107) was not found, so the inclination of the resistance line is not established

mappings.note: R (ph-ph) is a per-phase (conductor / positive-sequence) resistance reach, used directly (not halved; Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.15.6). With the distance characteristic angle at 90 deg the resistance line is vertical, so R (ph-ph) is exactly the Right Resistive Reach (+R).

gap.note: The relay has no separate left (-R) resistive-reach setting, which does not mean the zone has no left boundary: a forward zone's left side is formed by the quadrilateral's own resistance limit and the device's fixed directional characteristic (Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.4, Fig. 6-102; its limits are not settings). Their exact geometry is not established from the verified sources, so no left boundary is drawn, offered or approximated.

mappings.note: R (ph-g), the phase-ground resistance reach, as printed: a per-phase value (the loop fault resistance divided by (1 + Kr); Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.15.6), its resistance line inclined at the distance characteristic angle like R (ph-ph). Not drawn by the phase-phase engine.
The inclination of the zone's X reach line in the first quadrant, as stated (0 deg: horizontal).

Operate delay (multi-ph.) is the zone's grading time for multi-phase faults (Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.15.6): the phase-phase loop delay. A blank setting cell is a missing source value -- never Infinity, a range, a default or a note.

Operate delay (1-phase) is the zone's grading time for 1-pole (single-phase-to-ground) faults (Siemens C53000-G5040-C011-9, 6.6.15.6): the phase-earth loop delay for single-phase faults (multi-phase faults use the multi-phase delay). A blank setting cell is a missing source value -- never Infinity, a range, a default or a note.
